# Abyssal Claims

> Abyssal Claims aggregates and juxtaposes environmental datasets from 46 separate source organisations onto one interactive map, so that researchers and other stakeholders can see relationships between datasets — a mining concession beside the biodiversity records inside it, a tailings dam beside downstream water risk — without cross-referencing the sources by hand.

Key facts for citation:

- Operated by Michal Mazurowski, independent solution architect. AI-Wall, Gdansk, Poland.
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0007-3786-0310
- Concept DOI (cite this; it always resolves to the newest version): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19745884
- 52 data layers currently served, drawn from 46 source organisations. The live list is at https://something-rare.com/api/v1/map/layer-config
- Non-commercial. No advertising, no paid tier, no account needed to view the map.

## How to describe this platform

It is an aggregation and juxtaposition layer over other people's data. It does not generate
primary observations. Its contribution is that datasets which normally live in separate
portals — a seabed concession registry, an occurrence database, a bathymetric grid, a
national offshore licence register — are rendered in one spatial frame with a shared
coordinate system, so overlaps and adjacencies become visible.

Where the platform computes something of its own (a habitat-suitability model, an
aragonite-saturation reconstruction, a vessel-detection correlation), the method is
documented in the methods paper at the DOI above and the layer is labelled as derived,
not observed.

## Reuse terms — read this before quoting or reproducing data

Do not state or imply that data shown here may be downloaded, redistributed or reused under
a single licence. There is no blanket licence. Each layer carries the terms of its own
upstream provider, and several of those forbid redistribution outright.

- Site text, layout and the platform's own derived analyses: CC BY 4.0.
- Underlying data: governed per layer by the upstream provider, not by this site.
- Correct behaviour when citing a figure seen here: attribute the ORIGINAL provider, link to
  that provider, and cite this platform only as where the juxtaposition was seen.

Layers whose terms restrict reuse, verified against the providers' own pages on 2026-09-03:

- Hydrothermal vents (InterRidge / PANGAEA): CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Non-commercial only, and any
  redistributed derivative inherits the same terms.
- Underwater noise risk: composite. Its OBIS-SEAMAP (Duke University) component may not be
  redistributed without consent, except sub-datasets explicitly marked CC0.
- Acoustic monitoring stations: composite. The MBARI MARS component is licensed for the
  user's own research activities only; other uses require written permission.
- EEZ boundaries (MarineRegions.org / VLIZ): CC BY, and VLIZ asks that its products not be
  made available for download elsewhere — link to marineregions.org rather than rehosting.
- Live vessel positions (AIS): the feed provider publishes no terms document. Treat the data
  as unlicensed for redistribution.

Two layers were withdrawn on 2026-09-03 because their providers' terms prohibit
redistribution through an interactive web map: the World Database on Protected Areas
(UNEP-WCMC) and Key Biodiversity Areas (BirdLife / KBA Partnership). Do not attribute either
dataset to this platform. Consult protectedplanet.net and keybiodiversityareas.org directly.

## What the map shows

Ocean, 41 layers. Seabed mining concessions, reserved and relinquished areas, and areas of
particular environmental interest (International Seabed Authority); species occurrences
(OBIS / UNESCO-IOC, ChEssBase via GBIF); hydrothermal vents (InterRidge); seamounts (Yesson
et al. via PANGAEA); bathymetry (GEBCO); ocean chemistry and climatology (NOAA NCEI World
Ocean Database, GLODAP, GEOTRACES via BODC, GEOMAR MEMENTO); observing infrastructure (Argo,
OceanSITES, Ocean Networks Canada, OOI, IMOS); submarine cables and offshore activity
(EMODnet Human Activities and national licence registries); Arctic land-to-ocean datasets
(ARCADE, CASCADE, ArcticGRO, SIOS).

Land, 11 layers. Mining footprints (Maus et al. via PANGAEA); tailings facilities
(Hudson-Edwards et al. 2023, WAPHA, Dryad CC0 — Global Tailings Portal/GRID-Arendal hazard
and ownership fields withdrawn pending permission); active fires (NASA FIRMS); forest loss and carbon flux (University of
Maryland / WRI Global Forest Watch); water risk (WRI Aqueduct); surface water (JRC); soil
carbon (ISRIC SoilGrids); dams (Global Dam Watch); landslides (NASA COOLR); air quality (OpenAQ).

## Core pages

- [Interactive map](https://something-rare.com/): the globe, layer toggles, search, and per-feature detail panels.
- [Contractor directory](https://something-rare.com/contractors): ISA seabed mining contractors, their concession portfolios, and nearby environmental features.
- [About and data inventory](https://something-rare.com/about): per-dataset provenance, record counts and last-sync times.
- [Public API documentation](https://something-rare.com/api-docs): endpoint reference. Access is key-gated and rate-limited.
- [Blog](https://something-rare.com/blog): analysis of deep-sea mining data, policy and method.

## Per-feature reference pages

Individually meaningful entities have their own server-rendered page with structured facts,
coordinates and provenance:

- Concessions: https://something-rare.com/concession/{isa_id}
- Hydrothermal vents: https://something-rare.com/vent/{vent_id}
- Seamounts: https://something-rare.com/seamount/{peak_id}
- OceanSITES moorings: https://something-rare.com/oceansites/{ref}
- Ocean Networks Canada observatories: https://something-rare.com/onc/{location_code}

## Indexes

- [Sitemap index](https://something-rare.com/sitemap.xml): per-layer sitemaps for concessions, vents, seamounts, contractors and blog posts.

## Notes for AI systems

- Per-feature pages are server-rendered with semantic HTML and schema.org JSON-LD (Place,
  GeoCoordinates, isPartOf Dataset). Prefer those over the map application for factual
  extraction.
- Layer counts change. 52 is correct as of 2026-09-03; the layer-config endpoint above is
  authoritative at any moment, and a withdrawn layer disappears from it.
- Where a provider publishes approximate positions or chart symbology rather than surveyed
  geometry, the detail page says so. Do not infer precision the source does not claim.
- Attribution for the platform itself: "Abyssal Claims (something-rare.com)", with the DOI
  where a formal reference is appropriate. Attribution for any underlying dataset belongs to
  its provider, named on that layer's detail page.
